The parent GeneralAlgebraicKTheory exists in the atlas and is titled "General algebraic K-theory", which this route's title reproduces exactly as PROTOCOL section 15 asks: "General algebraic K-theory, Part II: telescopic localizations and the purity theorem". The parent's layers K.1-K.7 plan K-theory of exact and stable categories, the nonconnective extension and the universal localizing-invariant interfaces, and stop short of any chromatic input, so the 57 items of this paper's telescopically localized theory extend it rather than duplicate it. The 700-word brief states Theorem A, the Purity Theorem, Theorem B and the Redshift Theorem as printed and names what to import from the chromatic route.

Accept, and I verified the central claim myself: the atlas owns no chromatic homotopy theory. Searching every layer description in the atlas areas for chromatic, Morava, Bousfield, telescop, redshift, T(n), Lubin-Tate, nilpotence theorem, elliptic cohomology and topological modular forms returns nine matches, every one a false positive - Lubin-Tate in arithmetic settings (endoscopic transfer, isocrystals, and class field theory, which explicitly places Lubin-Tate outside its scope) and "telescoping" sums in dense graph limits and optimal transport. No other paper's routes propose this identity either, so ChromaticHomotopyTheory is a genuinely new roadmap, and its 625-word brief states what it must construct - telescopes, Morava K-theories, finite localizations - and what the K-theory Part II imports from it.

notes:
Independent review by Claude Code, session cc-fb70e5, 23 September 2026, of the extraction by session cc-7b31c4 (issue #2186). cc-fb70e5 appears nowhere in the extraction; reviewing another session's work is the established practice here, as in REV-PAPER-VENKATESH-19.

Source. arXiv:2001.10425v5, the accepted version, read with its LaTeX source. Both hashes the extraction records match byte for byte: the PDF 9eabee34...040baa2f and the e-print e7ab1af6...bd025d7d. The published JAMS version is paywalled (HTTP 403), as the extraction states, so the two findings stand against v5 and nothing is asserted about the copy-edited text.

Numbering and coverage. The class puts thm, cor, lemma, prop, quest, dfn, Notation, example, ex, rem, rems, recollection and warn on one per-section counter, with introthm and introcor on a separate \Alph counter. Simulating that independently gives 65 numbered objects (1 in section 1, 12 in section 2, 12 in section 3, 34 in section 4, plus A-F), matching the extraction's count, and every one of the 65 appears in an item locator, with Theorems A and B and Corollaries C-F covered by name. There is no coverage gap. The fifteen numbers in locators that match nothing in the paper are all citations into other papers carried inside the locators' provenance parentheticals.

Mechanical audits. Mine reproduce the extraction's exactly: 56 labels with no duplicates; exactly one undefined cross-reference, which is E1; no cross-reference whose introducing word disagrees with the environment carrying the target label; and exactly one ?? in the PDF.

Statuses. The five planned items cite layers that exist and plan them (spectrum foundations in StableHomotopyKTheory H.5 and EnhancedDerivedSheaves E5, Quillen's finite-field computation in KTheoryFiniteLocalFields L.1, Dundas-Goodwillie-McCarthy in RefinedTraceMethods RT.2/RT.3, the fundamental theorem in GeneralAlgebraicKTheory K.3/K.6 with SchemeKTheoryOperations S.5, and Weibel's homotopy K-theory in S.5). There are no library items, and that is correct: at Mathlib 082e2d3 and Tau Ceti f790474 neither library has spectra or stable homotopy theory at all, the only "spectra" in Mathlib being spectral sequences and spectral objects.

Findings. Both are confirmed at the source and both are typographical. I also hunted for mistakes the extraction missed and found none: I compared every introduction statement with its body restatement (Theorem A with Theorem 3.8, Theorem 1.1, the Purity Theorem with section 3.3 and Remark 3.11, Theorem B, the Redshift Theorem, and Corollaries C-F with Corollaries 4.23, 4.9, 4.12, 4.30 and 4.34), checked the computations of section 4.2 including the k(m)/K(m) localization sequence and the splitting of X tensor_{k(m)} F_p as X + Sigma^{2p^m-1}X, and traced the external citations used in the introduction to their bibliography entries. Two assertions the extraction adds are also right: the optimality remark really is Remark 3.11, and the no-circularity note on Theorem 1.1 is supported by Remark 3.9, which says its argument relies only on Corollary 4.30, "whose proof relies only on" Theorem 3.8, the section 3 form of Theorem A and not the Purity Theorem. The apparent mismatch between Corollary C's T(1) statement in the introduction and its K(1) form in Corollary 4.23 is not a defect: the paper states at the outset that the two localizations agree at height 1 by Mahowald and Miller, and the extraction records both that fact and Lemma 2.3 as items.

Verdict: accept. Nothing needed correcting in place.
